title: Kingdom Chronicle
description:
Kingdom Chronicle is a turn-based conquest strategy game in which you lead one of many realms on a divided continent and set out to unify it. Area campaigns are decided in 30 minutes to an hour, and even the Grand Campaign takes only about 1–2 hours. The rules are few, and the core clicks quickly. That does not make it an easy game.■ Few Options, and Alliances Are the KeyCommands are grouped by category, and what each one does is clear. The strategic options are intentionally limited, and the key is alliances: whether you can form them and keep Trust high through Goodwill goes a long way toward deciding the outcome.
The Tutorial on the title screen (5 steps) walks you through the basics on a real board, from your first moves to alliances, preparing to march, your first battle, and defense and reinforcements. During play, your strategist advises you on the odds of success and on looming dangers, and for commands such as governance and military preparations, you can check a forecast of the results before carrying them out. After each battle, you can also review a breakdown of combat power.■ With Few Options, the AI Doesn't HesitateFew options means the AI doesn't hesitate either. The AI uses the same commands you do: it builds up its realm, forms alliances, sends reinforcements, and strikes the moment you show a weakness. Until you get the hang of it, you may be overrun before you know it. If you expect to need some time to find your footing, starting on Casual or Easy is a good choice.
This is not a hero's tale where mighty officers carry you to a satisfying win. It is a game of conquest in which you read the board with a limited hand. The stronger a realm grows, the more it invites headwinds such as uprisings and defecting allies, and that includes you. You can't relax until the last bastion falls.
On the other hand, once you grasp the core, you'll find yourself winning with surprising consistency. Some seasoned players say they barely notice the difference between difficulty levels. Lose and learn, learn and win. That cycle, played out in short campaigns, is what this game is about.■ Before You Buy, Try the Demo to See If It's for YouThis game is built around that back-and-forth and those short campaigns. In exchange, it does not include the following.
・A tactical map where you move units, or battles you control directly (battles resolve automatically)
・Domestic management for each bastion, building construction, or a tech tree
・Growing your officers through level-ups or equipment
・A long campaign where you spend dozens of hours building up a great nation
The free demo lets you play the Tutorial and one area campaign all the way through. It also includes every difficulty level and Imperium Mode. The core rules and systems are the same as in the full version. The full version adds the remaining scenarios, content that unlocks after you clear them, and features added later such as command result forecasts, the Archives, and Custom Difficulty, but the feel of the game doesn't change much.
If the demo doesn't click with you, the full version probably won't either.
Your demo save data carries over to the full version as is, as long as you play on the same PC.■ Imperium Mode (Recommended)In this mode, once the situation ripens, you can declare a decisive campaign for unification. The declaration dissolves every alliance, and complete unification becomes the only path to victory. The other powers stop fighting one another and unite against you. In turn, your war machine gains momentum, and you can take on new Lieutenants.
If you never declare, the game plays under the normal rules. You can also choose Steam Mode, which has no declaration, or Free Mode, which follows the rules of the original free version.■ Governance, Diplomacy, Intrigue, and Six Troop TypesDevelop your land to raise national power, conscript and train your army, and grant relief to keep order. Build Trust through Goodwill to form alliances, and break your enemies from within with schemes and poaching. Battles turn on the matchups of six troop types (the cavalry-archer-spear triangle plus swords, magic, and armor) and on the back-and-forth of marching, intercepting, and reinforcing.■ 168 Officers168 officers appear, each with their own stats, troop type, special skill, and personality. Officers you bring under your command by recruiting, poaching, or capturing are added to the Officer Codex when you clear an area campaign or fight through to its final turn.■ What's Included・Three area campaigns, plus the Grand Campaign spanning the entire continent
・Four difficulty levels (Casual / Easy / Normal / Hard). On Hard, the AI's income increases for an even tougher fight
・Casual and Easy are meant for players who need more time to get the hang of things. They include events that help you recover from a losing position, and Codex entries and unlocks such as the Grand Campaign and the Officer Forge are earned regardless of difficulty. They're also a good fit if you want to take your time collecting officers
・Once you clear a scenario, you can also choose Custom Difficulty, which lets you adjust settings such as whether alliances are allowed, AI aggression, and income (Steam Mode and Imperium Mode only; some records and achievements do not count)
・Victory conditions: unification, alliance victory, or being the largest power when time runs out
・Clearing the Grand Campaign unlocks the Officer Forge, which lets you bring officers of your own design into battle, and War of the Forgotten, in which only officers of ★3 or lower take the field
・In the Archives, you can enjoy the Music Room, where you can listen to tracks that played during your games, and the Event Gallery, where you can revisit illustrations of events you've seen
description_short: Turn-based conquest strategy in roughly 30-minute to 2-hour campaigns. Battles resolve automatically. Alliances are the key, but the AI also forms alliances, sends reinforcements, and strikes at any weakness. Try the free demo first.
